categories.name: Technical SEO
what_works: Clean, descriptive URL structure with no query parameters or redirect chains
Proper viewport configuration for mobile responsiveness
HTTPS correctly implemented with a valid SSL certificate
Traditional server-rendered HTML (non-SPA layout) - optimal for crawlability

findings.title: Missing robots.txt file
findings.description: The site currently has no robots.txt file (404 status), meaning crawl bots receive no guidance or pathways, and the sitemap location is not declared.
findings.recommendation: Create a robots.txt file at the root with standard directives and a pointer to the XML sitemap.

findings.title: Missing sitemap.xml file
findings.description: No XML sitemap is present on any common paths (sitemap.xml, sitemap_index.xml, sitemap-index.xml, etc.), meaning search engines must rely on slow, discovery-based link-following.
findings.recommendation: Generate an XML sitemap of all public URLs and submit it via Google Search Console.

findings.title: Missing canonical tag
findings.description: No <link rel="canonical"> tag was detected on the homepage, presenting a risk of duplicate content issues if similar content is served on other URL variants (e.g. non-www, HTTP, trailing slash).
findings.recommendation: Add a self-referencing canonical tag in the <head> of the homepage pointing to https://easyourtour.com/.

findings.title: Missing essential security headers
findings.description: The server response does not contain critical security headers (HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, CSP), leaving the site vulnerable to common threats like clickjacking and MIME-sniffing.
findings.recommendation: Configure security headers directly in the server block (NGINX/Apache) or hosting platform configuration.

findings.title: No IndexNow endpoint
findings.description: No IndexNow verification file or link tag is present, slowing down content discovery and indexation by non-Google search engines like Bing, Yandex, and Naver.
findings.recommendation: Generate an IndexNow API key, upload the verification text file, and include the indexnow link in the HTML header.

categories.name: Content Quality & E-E-A-T
what_works: High information density in existing copy (0.9 out of 1.0)
Zero repetition or filler content detected in copy blocks
Clear, readable formatting with modern visual presentation
No evidence of low-quality AI content patterns

findings.title: Thin content on the homepage
findings.description: The homepage contains only ~70 words of extracted text, which is significantly below the 500-word topical floor recommended for high-performing homepages.
findings.recommendation: Expand the homepage copy to 800-1,200 words covering services, detailed destination highlights, company story, and guest reviews.

findings.title: Weak experience, expertise, and authority signals
findings.description: There is a severe lack of visible author bios, guide credentials, staff certifications, travel license disclosures, travel diaries, or co-branded partnerships.
findings.recommendation: Add certified guide profiles, display association logos (e.g., IATA, local travel license), and create a travel blog with first-hand guides.

findings.title: Insufficient trust signals
findings.description: While the phone number and contact forms are available, there is no prominent physical address, secure booking badge, payment guarantee, or detailed refund and cancellation policy links.
findings.recommendation: Display a complete physical address and email in the footer; create dedicated 'About Us', 'Privacy Policy', and 'Cancellation/Refund Policy' pages with direct footer links.

findings.title: Low AI search engine citation readiness
findings.description: The copy relies on generic marketing phrases (e.g., 'unforgettable guided tours') rather than structured, quotable facts and data tables that AI search engines (like ChatGPT or AI Overviews) can cite.
findings.recommendation: Insert unique data points, statistics, and precise package details (e.g. 'small-group tours limited to 8 guests', '3 nights at Fairmont Baku').

findings.title: Complete absence of Schema.org structured data
findings.description: No structured data of any format (JSON-LD, Microdata, RDFa) was found, meaning search engines receive no machine-readable data about the travel agency, its destinations, packages, prices, or ratings.
findings.recommendation: Deploy valid JSON-LD scripts for WebSite, TravelAgency/Organization, TouristAttraction (destination pages), and TouristTrip + Offer + AggregateRating (tour pages).

categories.name: Performance
what_works: Incredible mobile Lighthouse performance score of 99/100
Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) is 1.6 seconds, well within the green threshold (<2.5s)
Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) is 0.03, showing outstanding visual stability (<0.1)

findings.title: Potential render-blocking resources
findings.description: A few Next.js critical static files and Google woff2 fonts can cause minor blocking on slow networks. No preload tags are currently defined for non-Next critical assets.
findings.recommendation: Use rel=preload for crucial custom fonts and audit third-party script deferral periodically.

phases.name: Phase 1: Critical Fixes
items: Create and upload a standard robots.txt file pointing to the sitemap.
Generate and submit a standard XML sitemap via GSC.
Configure standard security headers (HSTS, X-Frame-Options, etc.) on the server.

phases.name: Phase 2: Structured Data & Discovery
items: Implement TravelAgency/Organization JSON-LD on the homepage.
Deploy TouristTrip + Offer + AggregateRating schemas on popular tour landing pages.
Add BreadcrumbList structured data to improve SERP breadcrumb pathways.
Generate and set up the IndexNow endpoint for faster Bing/Yandex indexation.

phases.name: Phase 3: Content Expansion & E-E-A-T
items: Expand the homepage text block from ~70 words to 800-1,200 words covering key services and destinations.
Add trust signals to the footer: a physical address, secure booking badge, and transparent policies.
Feature guide profiles and certified travel agency license numbers to showcase expertise.
Embed co-branded logos of reputable travel partnerships and travel association memberships.

phases.name: Phase 4: AI Citation & Monitoring
items: Inject structured, quotable facts and data tables on tour pages to drive AI search engine citations.
Establish an active blog with first-hand travel guides and 'Travel Diaries' to signal real-world experience.
Monitor Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools for indexation status and crawling crawl-rate.
Perform monthly Lighthouse audits to verify the 99/100 performance score remains stable.
